title: Riverside Pavilion
summary: A low, cantilevered reading pavilion that lets the river walk straight through it.
brief: The brief asked for a small public room on a flood-prone riverbank. Rather than resist the water, the pavilion lifts onto a thin plinth and lets the ground slip beneath a deep cantilever, so the public path never stops. Light enters low and long; the timber core anchors what the glass dissolves.
note: The pavilion began as a question: can a public room disappear when the river rises, and reappear when it falls? Everything in the project answers that.

process.note: First idea in pencil — the roof as a single held gesture over the path.
Plan, section and elevation resolved in AutoCAD to test the cantilever depth.
1:100 balsa study to read the light under the overhang.
Digital massing to check proportion from the approach.
